info.name: RPOWER Core API
info.description:
An API to provide developers the ability to query data from the RPOWER Above-Store database.

Authorize to use API

To utilize the API, you will need an authorization token, which you can request from RPOWER by emailing a request to integrations@rpower.com. Once you have your authorization token, you can then pass it to each of the API endpoints by creating an Authorization HTTP Header and adding Bearer, space, and then your token, like so:

Authorization: Bearer Your_Token

First Things First

The first call to make is to one of the store endpoints, either http://rpowerpos.com/api/v1/coreapi/store/getbyserialnumber if you know the cg number and serial number of the store you are looking for, or http://rpowerpos.com/api/v1/coreapi/store/get to get the list of stores you can view with the API. Both calls will provide you with cg numbers and store mids for any subsequent calls you need to make

Customer and Customer Group Endpoint Access is Restricted

Due to security concerns for our customers' private information, to access the Customer and Customer Group endpoints, you must have signed an agreement from RPOWER stating that you will abide by our customer information usage policies. For more information, or for answers to any questions about our customer information policies, email integrations@rpower.com.

Note about time_stamp

The time_stamp value represents the time a record was written or updated. This value will be changed any time data is reposted from RPOWER at the store. When seeking records associated with a particular day/time associated with business activity, rely on date values instead of time_stamp values.

request.description:
Retrieves a set of close day records by business date range.

Required Parameters:

cg: The store's consolidation group number, many times the same as the store serial number.

storemid: The store's unique id.

startdate: The first date in the desired range.

enddate: The last date in the desired range.

Optional Parameters:

sortorder: Valid values for sortorder are: from_date, from_date_desc

pagenumber: The page number. We return 1000 records per page. So sending a 1 for the page number will get you the first 1000 records. Sending a 2 will get you records 2000-2999. This way,
you can fill lists at 1000 records at a time. If this parameter is not specified, you will only get back the first 1000 records.

description.content: (Required) The first date in the desired range.
(Required) The last date in the desired range.

(Optional) The page number based on 1000 records per page. For example, a request that includes pagenumber=1 will return the first 1000 records, a request that includes pagenumber=3 will return records 2000-2999, etc. If a pagenumber value is requested and no records populate that range of records, no results will be returned. If a pagenumber value is not specified, the response will include the first 1000 records.
